svg.title: Kritva Nexus internal connectivity view (preliminary planning diagram)
svg.desc: Masters, the four application AXI fabrics, the AXI fabric bridge on the C910 to APB route, the Memory Access Crossbar, the DDR4 controller, OSPI controllers, two AXI-to-APB interconnects, the separate secure AXI interconnect and the security domain, with each link tagged with its interface register identifier and label.
svg.text: four fabric ingress ports; arbitration, QoS, decode, protection
Isolation boundary: separation of the secure and application address spaces is OPEN (NX-REQ-028,
NX-INT-012); the application AXI has no access to security resources (NX-REQ-034 [P]). No crossing is drawn.
Separate secure AXI interconnect: concept [S] 032; 32-bit data and address, 2 outstanding reads and writes [P] 033 (NX-INT-011)
Clock, reset, power and always-on: control connections are not drawn (NX-INT-015, 017 to 019)
Not drawn because the registers do not define them:
- ISP to NPU data interface (NX-INT-006 [O]); frame ownership and release (NX-INT-007 [P]).
- C910 reset-release control by the security domain (NX-INT-014 [P], NX-REQ-037).
- Application address map (NX-REQ-053 [P]), address width (NX-REQ-029 [O]), address windows.
- Which fabric each OSPI controller attaches to; interrupt routing (NX-INT-016 [O]).
- DMA request lines, descriptor memory path and its register access through APB (NX-INT-023 [P], NX-ARCH-OI-035 [O]).
Fabric count [S] 015 (NX-DEC-014); roles and widths [P] 050; master placement [P] 051; APB bridges [S] 016.
Link style follows the label of its NX-INT entry; box style follows the label of the block.
PRELIMINARY PLANNING DIAGRAM, NOT A PRODUCT SPECIFICATION.
Derived from the requirements register and interface register; every label is the register label. INT-nnn means NX-INT-nnn.
Widths, frequencies and links marked [P] are proposals, not decisions. No timing, bandwidth or latency result exists.
